heart rate variability and vagal reflexes are important prognostic factors in patients with myocardial infarctions, and they should be considered in risk stratification.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ATRAMI data provide the first prospective clinical data that low BRS and heart rate variability are independent and additional predictors of postinfarction mortality and that they significantly add to the prognosticate value of ventricular arrhytmias and LVEF.

heart rate variability, baroreflex sensitivity, and LVEF are all independent prognostic markers after myocardial infation, and that the combination of these three variables may improve risk stratification.
the analysis of vagally mediated reflexes is an important component of risk stratification after myocardial infraction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the baroreflex is an independent prognostic marker in patients after MI, and that it adds prognostic information beyond that of LVEF, heart rate variability, and ventricular arrythmias.
the autonomic system is important in the development of heart failure and that the baroreflex system can be measured noninvasively.
